approach.method_basis: Particle swarm optimization runs a population of points that each remember where they have been. A particle keeps a position, a velocity, and the best position it has personally found, and each step its velocity is pulled by inertia toward its own past direction, by a stochastic attraction to its personal best, and by another to the best position the whole swarm has seen. Applied to molecules, the positions live in the continuous latent space of a molecular autoencoder, and every position is turned into a real molecule by a frozen decoder before being scored.
approach.novelty: This root commits to velocities that persist across the entire objective rather than being redrawn each round, so a particle carries momentum through many feedback batches. It attaches accepted scores to the exact latent position that generated the molecule, rather than to a re-encoding of it, which is what keeps the personal and social memories geometrically honest when the decoder is many-to-one.

hypothesis: Move persistent particles through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE latent space using inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward their own best observed position and the swarm best observed position, and attach accepted molecular scores to the exact generating positions before updating those task-local memories.

finding_summary.headline: Swarm dynamics reproduced across seeds as final scores fell
finding_summary.insights: The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. The initial identity gate prevented all supplied initial scores from becoming attractors in the new seeds; shared memory was then established from the first accepted batch and used normally thereafter. That separates safe score handling from the decoder's limited ability to recover the supplied molecules. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. The loss of the stronger aromatic/basic-amine family accompanies the largest score decline, but the data do not isolate its cause. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. Representation quality and motion scale remain separate questions for controlled follow-up. The execution finding is specific to the evaluated CUDA runtime: all runtime repeat-decodes matched, while independent CPU replay changed the decoded identity on 16 of 2,932 new motion attempts. Cross-backend decoder identity is therefore not established.
finding_summary.results: The two additional seeds reproduced the intended persistent motion, accepted-score memories and information transfer. All 2,932 motion equations and state transitions were verified, including 2,732 reuses of persistent velocity. Cognitive attraction was nonzero in all 1,896 eligible distinct-position opportunities, social attraction in all 2,801 eligible opportunities, and real shared memories influenced other particles 2,700 times. Accepted proposals established 200 personal bests and strictly improved them 658 times; every updated personal memory with a later opportunity was reused. All 2,900 proposals were accepted with no evaluator invalids or duplicates, and every generating position matched its runtime repeated decode. Mean final-best scores were 0.450789 in the original seed, 0.358719 in the first new seed and 0.288163 in the second. The three-seed mean is 0.365890 with a population standard deviation of 0.066585. Most of the variation comes from drd2_docking, whose final scores fell from 0.859171 to 0.476176 and 0.124923. The three-seed means for the other objectives are 0.345495 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.569962 for deco_hop, 0.174178 for median_2 and 0.253060 for sitagliptin_mpo. The decoder learned in each preparation: new-seed heldout reconstruction losses fell from 4.565228 to 0.629885 and from 4.534641 to 0.633075. Exact heldout molecular reconstruction remained only 6/480 and 7/480. None of the 100 initial encoding receipts in the new runs reconstructed its original identity, so all 200 particles correctly began without scored attractors.

molecular.headline: Polyene-rich molecules with irregular ring systems and reactive polar groups; conventional aromatic–amine arrangements are unevenly represented
molecular.overall_character: This report covers the supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories, compared with seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node. All five tasks are represented, each by 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally varied but dominated by alternating double bonds, enol ethers, aldehydes, conjugated carbonyls and irregular medium-sized or large ring closures. Phenyl, thiophene and occasional nitrogen heteroaromatic fragments are present, but many compounds combine them with nonaromatic polyenes or unusually connected rings rather than conventional medicinal scaffolds. Ring-closure indicator rates are 0.8897–0.9724, whereas aromatic-atom indicators are only 0.5517–0.8172. Rings are therefore abundant without being uniformly aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.5 to 62.5, with a maximum of 147 on one task. These text lengths are not molecular weights. The cumulated-double-bond counter ranges from 0.0 to 0.05; it does not count the many ordinary alternating polyenes visible throughout the trajectories. The compounds contain useful amide, sulfone, amine and aromatic elements, but synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because long conjugated linkers, aldehydes, unusual sulfur/nitrogen valence patterns and complicated closures recur even among favorable examples. Some smaller conventional-looking compounds occur, so this is not a claim that every structure is unmakeable. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0, and the cited polyenes also leave alkene geometry unspecified. Graph validity and a favorable scalar score do not establish an isolable chemical form, stability or a defined three-dimensional structure.

per_task.generated_character: The high group consists of moderately sized but unusual conjugated ring systems: an S-imino diene ring attached to an aminated unsaturated carbon ring with carboxamide and thienyl enone groups, a fused unsaturated lactam/thioether system bearing a fluoroaniline, and hydrazone-containing or charged nitrogen structures. Aldehydes, amides, nitro groups, thioethers and enamine-like connections recur. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9552, aromatic_atom_rate 0.631 and mean SMILES length 40.5. Ring perception of the best structure gives a nonaromatic medium carbon ring rather than an ordinary phenyl or azaaryl core. Synthetic routes and stereochemical forms would be materially less straightforward than those of the initial indole carboxamide.
liabilities: The highest-scoring structure combines an unusual S-imino ring with an enone, while another high scorer carries O=[N+]=N. Their chemical forms and reactivity require separate assessment.

Aldehydes, thioesters, conjugated enamines and multiple unspecified double-bond geometries complicate stability and synthesis. Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.05, in addition to the frequent alternating polyenes.
The worst proposals introduce substantial size, flexibility or tightly connected ring complexity without retaining favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of compact, conventional aromatic and polar ring systems is missing from much of the output; ring closure is often achieved through extended unsaturated or irregular fused frameworks instead.

Stable and geometrically defined alternatives to the conjugated aldehyde/enamine and unusual S=N or O=[N+]=N motifs are insufficiently represented around otherwise favorable size and polar-group combinations.
No unique missing target motif follows from the chemically heterogeneous high group, and stereochemical sensitivity is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The S-imino/polyene/carboxamide structure scores 0.3565472174010858 and the fluoroaniline/lactam/thioether structure scores 0.34302515021197216. The initial conventional indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.37483330611175764 was also an unsaturated lactam bearing polar nitrogen functionality and an aromatic nitrile/carboxamide region, so the replication retains the same broad conjugated/polar character while changing connectivity. At the bottom, very large alkylated or ring-extended molecules score 1.1533920765551684e-30 and 8.812272454079934e-27; a long arylalkyl amine/polyene scores 3.8438521003485694e-25. The initial tiny alkyl bromide is also very low at 8.305895500294491e-10. The observable preference is a bounded size with aromatic/polar features, not unrestricted extension or truncation. The median is 0.042253, and late seed-2 oxygen/sulfur-rich polyenes remain modest, including 0.09723031993424279 and 0.03267406883416671. The high scores do not identify a uniquely required ring system or establish that the unusual functionalities are beneficial in isolation.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is dominated by very elaborated polyaryl amides, ureas, nitroaryl groups and fluorinated phenyl rings, sometimes joined into large conjugated or cyclophane-like systems. The best structure encodes an unusually large conjugated nitrogen/carbonyl ring with fused aromatic portions and unsaturated side arms. Other high examples are long chains of phenyl rings connected to amides and nitrobenzophenone-like regions. Seed 2 includes additional irregular fused or bridged polar rings. Mean SMILES length is 62.5 and the maximum is 147; ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.7638. These are mostly large, synthetically demanding structures, with only a modest numerical separation from the initial screening-like molecules.
liabilities: Multiple nitroaryl groups and extensive conjugated or polyaryl surfaces introduce physicochemical and reactivity questions that the score does not answer.
A relatively high-scoring structure contains an acyl fluoride, which is chemically distinct from ordinary aryl fluorination.
Large irregular ring closures, unspecified polyene geometry, a late peroxide linkage and hydrogen-bearing sulfur functionality make many examples demanding synthetic or chemical-form targets.
missing_features: Compact, well-defined arrangements of aromatic nitrogen, donor/acceptor groups and linkers are unevenly represented; much of the output adds phenyl rings, polyenes and carbonyl groups instead.

Chemically comparable alternatives around the low-scoring nonaromatic sulfone systems are missing as an interpretable local series. The baseline shows that sulfone removal cannot be prescribed universally.
The high group does not reveal a unique missing decoration or geometry, and a small score difference from the initial molecules does not establish a need for its much greater structural complexity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large conjugated polycarbonyl/N-containing ring system scores 0.5620451020164658, the polyaryl amide/urea with nitro groups scores 0.5619777544131481, and the extended oligophenyl amide scores 0.5607123583378306. The initial fused-dione ester already scores 0.548381482770623, compared with a reported median of 0.520067. The visible gradient therefore tolerates extensive aromatic and polar-group elaboration without demonstrating that such complexity is necessary. The seed-0 best scored 0.5927058823529412 and combined a nitrogen-rich aromatic ring, a sulfone and aryl imine/amine links; the new high group shifts toward larger carbon-rich aromatic/amide assemblies. All six digest worst proposals contain carbon-bonded sulfones in largely nonaromatic unsaturated surroundings, with the worst at 0.25506553536376875. The higher-scoring baseline sulfone prevents attributing this contrast to sulfone presence alone. Late seed-2 sulfone/polyene structures continue near 0.26–0.28, while a different fused aminal/heteroaryl structure reaches 0.5551363900174116. These are unpaired chemical contrasts, not proof of a required substituent or a forbidden functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The new high-scoring molecules are chiefly chlorinated arylalkyl hydrocarbons with long alkyl or conjugated links. The best contains chlorinated phenyl groups and a chlorinated diene, with no nitrogen or oxygen. Other upper examples add a phenol, aldehyde, ether or an enamine-like amino arm; a partially unsaturated aryl-substituted nitrogen ring appears below them. This is a largely lipophilic, halogen-rich population rather than a dense family of conventional basic cyclic amines. Mean SMILES length is 55.5, halogen_rate 0.8948, ring_closure_rate 0.9276 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6724. The arylalkyl chemistry can be recognizable, but long links and unusual heteroatom-rich late structures weaken general drug-likeness.
liabilities: The high nitrogen-free arylalkyl molecules combine extensive halogenation and hydrophobic surface with few polar groups, raising solubility and nonspecific-partitioning questions without establishing either outcome.
Conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers and halogenated unsaturation recur. Late proposals add very unusual sulfur or organophosphorus forms, including a difluorophosphoryl group, without favorable scores.
Long chains and large irregular closures increase conformational ambiguity; the score alone does not supply a binding geometry.
missing_features: The combined exposed aliphatic amine and bounded aromatic/spacer arrangement seen in the favorable baseline is poorly represented in the new high group, even though the generator can make amines.
The new examples do not provide a controlled comparison of linker length, amine availability and aromatic substitution; adding nitrogen indiscriminately would not follow from the shown scores.
Defined configurations and alkene geometries are absent in molecules whose flexible or substituted links can change their spatial arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl/diene scores 0.4761756997497859, and the more extended chlorinated arylalkyl structure scores 0.3966137972553488. An amino/phenol/aldehyde-containing relative scores 0.35740480261120694. The current high group therefore associates the visible signal with connected hydrophobic aromatic surfaces; it does not itself demonstrate a mandatory amine. The supplied seed-0 baseline is informative: its best at 0.8591709360377655 paired a free tertiary alkylamine with a brominated fused aromatic region, and another tertiary-amine-containing structure scored 0.7578688791540653. The new upper group largely lacks that combination. Current low examples include a small fluorinated enol-ether ester at 0.00010990702906285781, a conjugated aryl aldehyde at 0.00012492407267700092 and an amide-containing biphenyl at 0.00012620521493077546. Aromatic or halogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.022728, and the final sulfonamide/polyene or oxygen-rich structures remain low. The baseline comparison supports exploring exposed amines in suitable aromatic surroundings, while remaining insufficient to claim a particular receptor interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable seed-2 molecules are relatively compact combinations of aromatic rings and polar cyclic groups. The best joins benzodioxole through an amino link to a methoxy/methyl-substituted seven-membered N-containing carbonyl ring; the latter should not be called an ordinary six-membered pyridone. Other high examples include a diaryl sulfone with an oxygen-rich fused medium ring and a benzodioxole-containing cyclic hydrazone/lactam. Seed 1 more often emits enlarged fused carbonyl/imine systems with alkyl appendages. Mean SMILES length is 43.6, ring_closure_rate 0.9724 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8172. The smaller upper examples have recognizable chemical components, but uncommon ring topology and more elaborate lower-scoring structures keep makeability uncertain.
liabilities: The unusual seven-membered aromatic carbonyl ring and cyclic hydrazone require attention to tautomeric form and geometry rather than treatment as routine six-membered heteroarenes.

Other proposals combine aldehydes, N–O connections, ester/acetal-rich medium rings and highly unsaturated small rings. These features create stability or synthetic questions even when ring and aromatic indicators are positive.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, chemically conventional versions of the favorable aromatic/polar arrangements is limited; many alternatives instead become long polyenes or irregular medium-ring systems.
A unique missing reference-like structure cannot be inferred from the narrow score separation and chemically different upper examples.
Stereochemical and double-bond geometry specification is absent in the substituted saturated and hydrazone/polyene structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzodioxole/amino/aza-carbonyl-ring compound scores 0.18685638443799904, the diaryl sulfone scores 0.17882042440964765 and the cyclic hydrazone/lactam scores 0.17816898171823184. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. That initial molecule was also the seed-0 overall best; the highest seed-0 optimizer proposal was an unsaturated macrocyclic lactam at 0.14023138978580565. Thus the favorable new chemistry is somewhat more compact and organized around aromatic/polar ring combinations than the baseline generated high end. The lowest current examples are a small dibromoalkane at 0.014314958357846713 and acyclic unsaturated acid, aldehyde and enol-ether structures around 0.018–0.021. This supports aromatic ring architecture with appropriately arranged polar functionality over simple polyene fragments or heteroatom count alone. The median is 0.111326. The last proposals range from a small oxygen heterocycle at 0.0464643845937283 to a complex amide/lactam at 0.17194608615974535, so favorable chemistry is not tied to a single ring family or monotonically increasing size.

per_task.generated_character: The output favors moderately sized but highly unsaturated carbonyl/N/O-rich structures: an N-methoxy nitrogen-rich cyclic amide with a benzoyl group and an aldehyde arm, aryl amides bearing imidates and explicit alkoxides, sulfonamide/enamide chains and unsaturated lactam-containing rings. Many structures have few or no aromatic rings; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.5517 and ring_closure_rate 0.8897. Mean SMILES length is 40.7 and halogen_rate only 0.069. The chemistry is therefore substantially different from a uniformly fluorinated aromatic library. Ordinary amide or phenyl fragments are embedded in numerous unusual, potentially labile molecular forms.
liabilities: The best molecule contains an N–O connection, an N–N connection and a conjugated aldehyde; these introduce stability, oxidation and isomeric-form questions.
Explicit benzyl alkoxide or deprotonated oxygen species occur among favorable examples. Their protonation state and isolable form cannot be inferred from their score.

Repeated enol ethers, imidates, alpha-dicarbonyls and enamine-like connections make the population chemically reactive or tautomerically ambiguous. The large polyene and polyacetal extremes additionally impose size or flexibility burdens.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently reproduce the particular bounded connectivity that separates the favorable cyclic compound from its closely related open-chain form.
Chemically stable, well-specified alternatives to the alkoxide, N–O/N–N, imidate and conjugated-aldehyde arrangements are insufficiently demonstrated around the favorable polar skeletons.

The trajectories do not justify a claim that a specific fluorinated fragment or basic amine is missing from an obligatory target motif. The larger limitation is control of topology, polarity and chemical form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-methoxy cyclic amide with an N–N connection, benzoyl group and conjugated aldehyde scores 0.2687964912603012. A closely related open-chain compound evaluated last scores 0.040358516578188335, providing a useful contrast in connectivity with largely overlapping functional groups. The aryl amide/imidate/benzyl-alkoxide structure scores 0.23418129517000225, and a nonaromatic unsaturated bicyclic amide with a sulfonamide arm scores 0.23098874100279387. Neither aromaticity nor fluorination is a universal high-end feature here. The seed-0 best at 0.259395205519374 was another carbonyl-rich unsaturated amide chain attached to a brominated unsaturated carbocycle. Both baseline and replication favor particular moderately sized polar/unsaturated arrangements, without establishing that the reactive functionality itself is required. At the bottom, a much larger fluorinated polyene scores 5.931767096585795e-76 and an oxygen-rich polyacetal macrocycle scores 1.8652722566013391e-41. Adding unsaturation, fluorine or oxygen alone does not help. The median is 0.000248, and most final carbonyl-rich structures also remain very low, so even abundant amides and aldehydes do not reliably reproduce the favorable connectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure indicators remain high at 0.8897–0.9724 while aromatic indicators range only from 0.5517 to 0.8172. The digest repeatedly shows nonaromatic polyene rings, long unsaturated chains and complicated closures. Several extended examples score near zero, whereas smaller aromatic/polar combinations score favorably. A cyclic nitrogen-rich compound scores 0.2687964912603012 and its closely related open-chain form 0.040358516578188335, showing that connectivity can matter beyond functional-group inventory.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator often substitutes long conjugated links and irregular large rings for bounded, chemically conventional scaffold architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable bounded ring sizes, controlled linker lengths and chemically conservative changes in ring connectivity around observed favorable structures. Preserve the ability to explore nonaromatic rings while distinguishing purposeful ring architecture from unchecked chain extension or closure complexity; let current task-local observations choose useful topology and size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest high or late examples contain conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers, imidates, thioesters, an acyl fluoride, unusual S=N and O=[N+]=N functionality, N–O/N–N links and explicit alkoxides. These occur alongside useful amide, sulfone and aromatic features rather than only among the lowest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Favorable polar-group combinations are not consistently supplied in stable, well-defined chemical forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conservative functional-group and oxidation-state alternatives within related skeletons and preserve explicit, chemically coherent hydrogen and charge states. Use local observations to test alternatives instead of assuming that a favorable scalar objective establishes stability or that all ionizable, sulfur-containing or carbonyl groups should be removed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied baseline includes a tertiary alkylamine attached to a halogenated fused aromatic region at 0.8591709360377655. The corresponding new high group is dominated by nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl compounds, with a best of 0.4761756997497859. Amines are present elsewhere, and some favorable carbonyl-rich molecules do not need an exposed amine, so simple amine absence or universal amine addition would misread the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably combine exposed aliphatic amines with bounded aromatic and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled placement of unacylated aliphatic nitrogens, together with variations in aromatic attachment and spacer length, while retaining other favorable scaffold features. Let current task-local feedback determine when exposed basicity is useful rather than prescribing it for every objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. The cited structures include substituted saturated ring junctions, branched side chains, hydrazones and many polyenes whose SMILES do not specify the relevant configuration or alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometrically complex saturated and unsaturated structures are emitted without configuration specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configurationally defined variants accessible and preserve their identities through generation and canonicalization. Assess them only through the current task observations; the files establish missing specification, not which stereoisomer is preferable or whether a particular score is stereosensitive.

method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

activation_observables.measurement: Compare token-normalized reconstruction NLL before training and at the selected checkpoint on the same fixed heldout sequences and latent-noise probes, reporting KL separately. Log train/holdout counts, vocabulary coverage, training steps, posterior-mean variation, greedy canonical reconstruction fraction, checkpoint reload equality and checkpoint hash. Expected learning is lower heldout reconstruction NLL than the untrained model; the checkpoint-selection holdout is not an independent test set. At every objective init and feedback boundary, verify unchanged encoder/decoder parameter hashes and zero trainable neural parameters. Imperfect reconstruction alone does not violate this representation contract.

activation_observables.measurement: For each particle initialization record the original observed identity and score, exact encoded position, deterministic reconstruction, identity-match flag and whether a scored attractor was admitted. Log absent attractors explicitly. For every accepted offspring join submitted identity, canonical identity, particle id, exact generating position, decoder hash and real score, then repeat deterministic decoding of that position. Reconstruct attractor admissions from these receipts. Expected invariants are zero scores assigned to mismatched initial reconstructions or unqueried points, matching repeated decoded identities, no reencoding substituted for a generating position, and one real score attached to its actual molecular position.
activation_observables.name: initial_identity_gating_and_exact_scored_position_receipts

activation_observables.measurement: Log every motion with stable particle id, source position and velocity, personal/shared best positions and receipt versions, coefficients, separate cognitive/social uniform draws, all three vector contributions, raw velocity, bound corrections, actual displacement and destination position. Recompute velocity and position equations and reuse of each particle's prior actual velocity; report residuals and contribution norms. Count nonzero inertia, cognitive and social terms among eligible opportunities, separating bootstrap, missing-attractor and coincident-position cases. Verify current position can differ from personal best and later moves retain its trajectory state. An attraction term need not be nonzero when its corresponding displacement is zero.
activation_observables.name: persistent_inertial_cognitive_social_particle_motion

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct each particle's chronological accepted scores and exact positions. Log personal-best receipts before and after feedback, first-best establishment versus strict improvement, score difference relative to the prior best, and deterministic handling of ties and rejected/unqueried points. Count real-scored admissions and strictly improving replacements separately; join updated versions to the same particle's later cognitive terms, excluding final admissions with no later opportunity. Expected activation is increasing real-scored memory admissions and later use, with best scores nondecreasing. Low strict-improvement frequency is score evidence; initial admissions must not be counted as strict improvements.
activation_observables.name: accepted_personal_best_memory_updates_and_reuse

activation_observables.measurement: At each feedback boundary log all eligible personal-best receipts, old/new shared-best identity, position, score, owner and version, and its recomputed maximum-score selection with tie rule. Link each next-batch social term to that resolved version, identifying use by particles other than the best's owner. Count cross-particle uses and uses of newly improved shared memories, distinguishing initialization, later accepted improvements and no-op ties. The reference is zero cross-particle social uses before motion; expected activation is later use of a real observed shared best with nonzero displacement when positions differ. No score or best from unresolved members of the current batch may affect its other proposals.
activation_observables.name: resolved_swarm_best_information_transfer

activation_observables.measurement: For every attempt log its particle, bootstrap or persistent-motion status, source/destination receipt, deterministic decoded canonical identity and invalid/seen/batch-duplicate outcome. Reconcile retries and emitted identities with exactly the init-announced batch size and verify every proposal retains particle-motion and frozen-decoder provenance. Record distinct particles, per-particle reuse, attempted and actual displacement norms, molecular fingerprint distances and accepted score changes relative to the particle's earlier personal best. Geometry and score changes are descriptive. Report unresolved terminal receipts separately. approach.method_basis: Particle swarm optimization runs a population of points that each remember where they have been. A particle keeps a position, a velocity, and the best position it has personally found, and each step its velocity is pulled by inertia toward its own past direction, by a stochastic attraction to its personal best, and by another to the best position the whole swarm has seen. Applied to molecules, the positions live in the continuous latent space of a molecular autoencoder, and every position is turned into a real molecule by a frozen decoder before being scored.
approach.novelty: This root commits to velocities that persist across the entire objective rather than being redrawn each round, so a particle carries momentum through many feedback batches. It attaches accepted scores to the exact latent position that generated the molecule, rather than to a re-encoding of it, which is what keeps the personal and social memories geometrically honest when the decoder is many-to-one.

finding_summary.insights: The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. approach.method_basis: Particle swarm optimization runs a population of points that each remember where they have been. A particle keeps a position, a velocity, and the best position it has personally found, and each step its velocity is pulled by inertia toward its own past direction, by a stochastic attraction to its personal best, and by another to the best position the whole swarm has seen. Applied to molecules, the positions live in the continuous latent space of a molecular autoencoder, and every position is turned into a real molecule by a frozen decoder before being scored.
approach.novelty: This root commits to velocities that persist across the entire objective rather than being redrawn each round, so a particle carries momentum through many feedback batches. It attaches accepted scores to the exact latent position that generated the molecule, rather than to a re-encoding of it, which is what keeps the personal and social memories geometrically honest when the decoder is many-to-one.

The swarm mechanism is refuted if positions or velocities are repeatedly replaced by independent proposals after bootstrap; if the inertia/cognitive/social equations or persistent velocity reuse are incorrect; if eligible nonzero attraction components are computed but never used; or if resolved shared memory never reaches other particles despite eligible distinct positions. A mismatched initial reconstruction receiving its original molecule's score, an unqueried point becoming a scored best, reencoding replacing the exact generating position, an incorrect best comparison, or unresolved within-batch score leakage refutes score-memory integrity. Changed neural weights, stochastic decoding, a learned objective surrogate, posterior-guided line search, graph/token mutation or molecule-library proposal substitution violates the root intent. Imperfect initial reconstruction, decoded plateaus, low personal-best improvement rates or no final Top-1 advantage do not alone refute correctly executed frozen-decoder particle dynamics; retain them as representation, search or score limitations.
